title: Zuni Café Roast Chicken with Bread Salad
headnote: The family rendition of the famous roast chicken from Zuni Café in San Francisco: a small bird salted days ahead, roasted very hot, and served over a warm bread salad that soaks up the pan juices. The soaked bread is the family favorite — don’t skimp on it.

items.raw: 4 small sprigs thyme, rosemary, or sage
¾ teaspoon fine sea salt per pound (about 2½ teaspoons)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
8 ounces day-old chewy country bread, crusts mostly removed
1½ tablespoons champagne or white wine vinegar, divided
1 tablespoon dried currants, soaked in 1 tablespoon warm water
2 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and 4 scallions, thinly sliced

steps.text: One to three days ahead, pat the chicken dry. Slide a herb sprig under the skin over each breast and thigh. Season all over with the salt and pepper, cover loosely, and refrigerate.

Heat the oven to 475°F. Tear the bread into 2- to 3-inch chunks, toss with 2 tablespoons oil, and toast on a sheet pan 5 minutes, until crisp on the edges. Tear into smaller pieces, toss with 3 tablespoons oil, 1 tablespoon vinegar, and a pinch of salt.
Put a 10-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat for a few minutes. Dry the chicken and set it in the pan breast side up — it should sizzle.

Roast 30 minutes, until the skin is browning. Flip it breast side down and roast 10 to 20 minutes more, then flip back breast side up for 5 to 10 minutes to recrisp the skin. It is done when the thigh reads 165°F.

While the chicken roasts, cook the garlic and scallions in 1 tablespoon oil until soft, and fold into the bread with the drained currants and pine nuts. Pile it in a shallow baking dish and put it in the oven for the last 5 to 10 minutes.

Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Pour off most of the fat, add a splash of water to the pan, and scrape up the browned bits. Drizzle the juices over the bread and toss with the greens and remaining vinegar.
Cut the chicken into pieces and set it on top of the bread salad with any last juices.

notes.label: Small bird, high heat
notes.text: the method only works with a 3- to 3½-pound chicken. Larger birds burn before they cook through.

notes.label: Smoke
notes.text: 475°F with chicken fat smokes. Clean the oven and turn on the fan first.

notes.label: Bread
notes.text: use chewy, open-crumb bread, not sourdough sandwich loaf. Day-old is better than fresh.

notes.label: The salt
notes.text: fine sea salt measures differently from kosher salt. If using Diamond Crystal kosher, use about 1¼ teaspoons per pound.

openQuestion: Who in the family makes this, and how did it become a family dish?
